<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Technology Segment  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our Technology segment continues to be a leader in the highly fragmented global eDiscovery market. Our international eDiscovery
operations were the primary driver of the organic growth in operating revenue in the Technology segment over the last three years. For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, operating revenue from
our Europe and Asia eDiscovery operations increased $12.4&nbsp;million to $73.7&nbsp;million, including $1.1&nbsp;million related to Iris, from $61.3&nbsp;million for 2014. Operating revenue
from our Europe and Asia eDiscovery operations were $50.3&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, operating revenue from our North America eDiscovery operations increased $35.5&nbsp;million to $271.9&nbsp;million, including
$27.8&nbsp;million related to Iris, from $236.4&nbsp;million for 2014, primarily due to an increase in document review billable hours offset by unit pricing pressures in our electronically stored
information ("ESI") service offerings and lower ESI data volumes. Operating revenue from our North America eDiscovery operations were $234.6&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Following
is a description of the significant sources of revenue in our Technology segment. </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Consulting, forensics and collection service fees based on the number of hours that services are provided. </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Fees related to the conversion of data into an organized, searchable electronic database. The amount earned varies primarily on the
number of documents produced or volume of data processed. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Hosting fees based on the amount of data stored. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Document review fees based on the number of hours spent reviewing documents, the number of pages reviewed or the amount of data
reviewed. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Fixed-fees related to our managed service eDiscovery solutions. </FONT></DD></DL>

Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration Segment  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The operating results of our Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration segment largely depend on the number, size, duration and
complexity of bankruptcy filings and of class action, mass tort, federal regulatory actions, data breach and litigation activity within the United States. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As
of the most recently reported data by the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, for the fiscal years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, there were approximately
0.84&nbsp;million, 0.94&nbsp;million and 1.07&nbsp;million new bankruptcy filings, respectively. </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Total bankruptcy filings for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 decreased 10% versus the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014.
During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, Chapter&nbsp;7 filings decreased 13%, Chapter&nbsp;11 filings increased by less than 1% and Chapter&nbsp;13 filings decreased 3%. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014, and 2013, Chapter&nbsp;11 bankruptcy filings represented 1% of total bankruptcy filings in the United States. While
Chapter&nbsp;11 cases represent the smallest number of U.S. bankruptcy filings, they represent the largest and most complex bankruptcy cases filed and require significant administrative support. Our
operating revenue from Chapter&nbsp;11 services represented 59%, 61% and 59% of total operating revenue from bankruptcy services for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013,
respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our
operating revenue from bankruptcy services decreased to $78.4&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from $83.0&nbsp;million for 2014, primarily due to a
decrease of $4.5&nbsp;million in revenue from Chapter&nbsp;11 services caused by a decline in early-case noticing revenues as compared to 2014. Operating revenue from bankruptcy services increased
to $83.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $79.7&nbsp;million for the same period of 2013, primarily due to the timing of a large Chapter&nbsp;11 engagement. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating
revenue from settlement administrative services increased to $81.9&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from $63.4&nbsp;million for 2014, primarily due
to large class action and data breach engagements during 2015. For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, our operating revenues from settlement administrative services decreased to
$63.4&nbsp;million from $74.0&nbsp;million for 2013, primarily due to a large anti-trust engagement that was completed in 2013. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
anticipate future operating revenue growth in our settlement administration business to be primarily driven by the demand for mass tort, federal regulatory action and data breach
related services. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Following
is a description of the significant sources of revenue in our Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration segment. </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Professional service fees and other support service fees contingent upon the month-to-month delivery of services, such as data
conversion, claims processing, claims reconciliation, project management, professional services, call center support, website development and administration, and controlled disbursements. The amount
we earn varies primarily on the size and complexity of the engagement. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Deposit-based fees earned on a percentage of Chapter&nbsp;7 assets placed on deposit with a designated financial institution by our
trustee clients, to whom we provide, at no charge, software licenses, limited hardware and hardware maintenance, and post-contract client support services. Service fees earned that are based on assets
placed on deposit by our trustee clients may vary based on fluctuations in short-term interest rates and changes in service fees assessed on such deposits. </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Legal noticing fees for services to parties of interest in bankruptcy, class action, and other administrative matters, including
direct notification and media campaign and advertising management in which we coordinate notification, primarily through print media outlets, to potential parties of interest for a particular client
engagement. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Data hosting fees and volume-based fees. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Monitoring and noticing fees earned based on monthly or on-demand requests for information provided through our AACER&reg;
software product. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Reimbursed expenses, primarily related to postage on mailing services and other pass-through expenses. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

Strategic and Financial Review  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On September&nbsp;18, 2014, the Company and its Board announced the commencement of a process to explore a full range of strategic
and financial alternatives, which may include among other things, acquisitions, divestitures, or a going-private or recapitalization transaction, in order to determine a course of action that is in
the best interest of all shareholders. There can be no assurance that the strategic review will result in the consummation of a transaction. We incurred $2.9&nbsp;million and $1.9&nbsp;million of
strategic and financial review expenses during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 and 2014, respectively. </FONT></P>

Revenue  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating revenue increased $61.8&nbsp;million, or 14%, to $505.9&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from
$444.1&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. This change is composed of an increase of $47.9&nbsp;million in the Technology segment, including $28.9&nbsp;million in
operating revenue from the acquisition of Iris and an increase of $13.9&nbsp;million in the Bankruptcy and </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Total
revenue includes reimbursable expenses, such as postage related to notification services and other third-party production costs. Although reimbursable expenses may fluctuate
significantly from period to period, these fluctuations have a minimal effect on our operating income as we realize little or no margin from this revenue. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Operating Expense  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Direct cost of operating revenue (exclusive of depreciation and amortization expense), increased $31.9&nbsp;million, or 15%, to
$248.2&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from $216.3&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. This was primarily due to an increase of
$14.3&nbsp;million related to Iris, an increase of $10.5&nbsp;million in production costs in our Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration segment primarily related to legal notification, print and
advertising expenses and call center related expenses, an increase of $6.6&nbsp;million in production costs in our Technology segment primarily related to software licenses, data hosting and
document review related expenses and an increase of $2.8&nbsp;million of direct compensation costs. These amounts were offset by a decrease of $2.3&nbsp;million in other direct miscellaneous
expenses, including $1.4&nbsp;million of expense related our data center consolidation project that was completed in 2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Reimbursable
expenses increased $6.6&nbsp;million, or 22%, during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 to $36.2&nbsp;million from $29.6&nbsp;million during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014. This corresponds to the 26% increase in revenue from Reimbursable expenses and is primarily due to higher postage volumes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Selling,
general and administrative expense increased $3.4&nbsp;million, or 2%, to $170.4&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from $167.0&nbsp;million
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. This was primarily due to an increase of $12.8&nbsp;million related to Iris, an increase of $9.3&nbsp;million in indirect employee compensation
costs, including $4.6&nbsp;million related to incentive compensation, and an increase of $1.7&nbsp;million related to external professional services and litigation expense. These increases were
offset by a decrease of $4.0&nbsp;million in bad debt expense, a decrease of $10.6&nbsp;million in postemployment benefits primarily related to employee severance charges, a decrease of
$2.9&nbsp;million in expense related to our data center consolidation project and a decrease of $2.7&nbsp;million in travel and entertainment expense. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Amortization
expense related to identifiable intangible assets increased $5.6&nbsp;million, or 44%, to $18.3&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from
$12.7&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. This increase was primarily related to the intangible assets acquired in connection with the Iris acquisition. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation
and software and leasehold amortization increased $1.8&nbsp;million, or 5%, to $37.8&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from
$36.0&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. This increase was primarily related to the property and equipment acquired in connection with the Iris acquisition. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
the year ended December&nbsp;31 2015, there was $1.2&nbsp;million of expense related to impairment of goodwill and identifiable intangible assets related to Minus
&#150;10 Software,&nbsp;LLC ("Minus 10"). See Note&nbsp;4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, there was $1.2&nbsp;million of income related to the fair value adjustment to contingent consideration related to the Minus 10 acquisition.
For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, there was $1.1&nbsp;million of expense related to the fair value adjustment to contingent consideration related to the De Novo Legal&nbsp;LLC
acquisition. See Note&nbsp;9 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other
operating expenses increased $4.4&nbsp;million to $5.3&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from $0.9&nbsp;million during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014. This increase was primarily related to an increase in acquisition-related expenses incurred in connection with the Iris acquisition. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Interest Expense  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense increased $3.7&nbsp;million, or 22%, to $20.4&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, from
$16.7&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. The increase was primarily due to higher principal amount of debt outstanding during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 to fund
the acquisition of Iris compared to 2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Income Taxes  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our effective tax rate is impacted by the applicable tax rate in jurisdictions where we generate pretax income (loss) and by the level
of pretax income (loss) generated. The primary international jurisdictions where we operate generally have a lower statutory rate than the United States. Our effective tax rate in the United States is
impacted by the valuation allowance against our net deferred tax assets and the amortization of tax basis in indefinite lived intangibles resulting in an increase to tax expense. The valuation
allowance in the United States and the resulting mix of income (loss) in the jurisdictions where we operate causes significant variations in our overall effective tax rate compared to the actual
statutory rates in the jurisdictions where we operate. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, our consolidated income tax expense was $19.6&nbsp;million compared to an income tax benefit of $4.5&nbsp;million for the same period of
2014. The increase in income tax expense was primarily due to a $17.0&nbsp;million valuation allowance established against our net deferred tax assets in the United States, including the deferred
tax assets generated as a result of our acquisition of Iris, and increased pretax income in our foreign jurisdictions. The primary factor that caused us to establish the valuation allowance was the
incurrence of cumulative pretax losses in the United States for the three year period ended December&nbsp;31, 2015. We had positive cumulative pretax earnings in the United States for the three year
period ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. See Note&nbsp;10 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information relating to the valuation allowance. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
income tax benefit of $4.5&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 was primarily the result of pretax losses incurred in the United States, partially offset by
pretax income in our foreign jurisdictions that have lower income tax rates than statutory tax rate in the United States. </FONT></P>

<A NAME="page_dm12601_1_32"> </A>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A HREF="#bg12601a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Technology Segment  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating revenue increased $47.9&nbsp;million, or 16%, to $345.6&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from
$297.7&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. The increase was primarily due to $28.9&nbsp;million of revenue from our acquisition of Iris, an increase of
$11.3&nbsp;million in Europe and Asia eDiscovery revenues as the result of growth in both ESI and document review revenues and an increase of $11.2&nbsp;million in document review revenues in
North America as the result of an increase in document review billable hours. These increases were offset by a decrease of $3.5&nbsp;million in North America ESI revenues caused by unit pricing
pressures for our ESI services combined with lower ESI data volumes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue
from reimbursable expenses decreased $0.5&nbsp;million, or 20% to $2.0&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from $2.5&nbsp;million during the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, primarily due to a decrease in reimbursable third party production costs. Our direct costs associated with reimbursable expenses are included in Direct costs, selling,
general and administrative expenses in the table above. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Direct
costs, selling, general and administrative expenses increased $35.9&nbsp;million, or 16%, to $254.2&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from
$218.3&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. This was primarily due to an increase of $26.9&nbsp;million related to Iris, an increase of $7.9&nbsp;million in employee
compensation expenses, including $5.5&nbsp;million related to project-based attorneys and contractor labor and an increase of $6.6&nbsp;million in production costs primarily related to third party
software, data hosting and lease cost for document review services. These increases were offset by a decrease of $3.6&nbsp;million in bad debt expense, a decrease of $1.1&nbsp;million in
miscellaneous general and administrative expenses such as utilities, professional services and office supplies, a decrease of $0.6&nbsp;million in reimbursable productions costs and a decrease of
$0.3&nbsp;million in travel and entertainment expenses. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration Segment  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating revenue increased $13.9&nbsp;million, or 9%, to $160.3&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from
$146.4&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. This was primarily due to an increase of $18.4&nbsp;million in settlement administration revenue driven by the timing of large
class action and data breach engagements, offset by a decrease in Chapter&nbsp;11 bankruptcy revenue of $4.5&nbsp;million primarily due to a decline in early-case noticing revenues as compared to
2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue
from reimbursable expenses increased $8.4&nbsp;million, or 30%, to $36.2&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from $27.8&nbsp;million during the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, primarily due to an increase in reimbursable postage costs. Our direct costs associated with reimbursable expenses are included in Direct costs, selling, general and
administrative expenses in the table above. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Direct
costs, selling, general and administrative expenses increased $21.4&nbsp;million, or 18%, to $142.5&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 from
$121.1&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. This increase was primarily due to an increase of $10.5&nbsp;million in legal notification costs, call center related costs,
print and advertising costs and other production-related expenses, an increase of $7.2&nbsp;million in reimbursed direct costs, primarily postage costs and an increase of $4.8&nbsp;million in
employee compensation expenses, including $0.6&nbsp;million related to incentive compensation. These increases were offset by a decrease of $0.7&nbsp;million in miscellaneous general and
administrative expenses such as utilities, professional services and office supplies, a decrease of $0.4&nbsp;million in bad debt expense and a decrease of $0.3&nbsp;million in travel and
entertainment expenses. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Revenue  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating revenue increased $5.4&nbsp;million, or 1%, to $444.1&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from
$438.7&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The increase in operating revenue was driven by a $12.8&nbsp;million increase in the Technology segment, offset by a
$7.4&nbsp;million decrease in operating revenues for the Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration segment. Refer to the subsequent Results of Operations by Segment for additional information. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Total
revenue includes reimbursable expenses, such as postage related to notification services and other third-party production costs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Operating Expense  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Direct cost of operating revenue (exclusive of depreciation and amortization expense), increased $5.8&nbsp;million, or 3%, to
$216.3&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $210.5&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The increase reflects the increase in and the mix of </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>33</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>
<!-- ZEQ.=3,SEQ=36,EFW="2227381",CP="EPIQ SYSTEMS,INC.",DN="1",CHK=867141,FOLIO='33',FILE='DISK134:[15ZCW1.15ZCW12601]DM12601A.;26',USER='SLYUBOM',CD='18-FEB-2016;13:46' -->
<A NAME="page_dm12601_1_34"> </A>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A HREF="#bg12601a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>operating
revenue and includes a $15.6&nbsp;million increase in direct compensation costs primarily in our Technology segment. This increase was partially offset by a $9.3&nbsp;million decrease in
costs for legal notification and advertising services. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Reimbursable
expenses decreased $12.2&nbsp;million, or 29%, during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 to $29.6&nbsp;million from $41.8&nbsp;million during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease corresponds to the percentage decline in revenue from Reimbursable expenses and is primarily due to lower postage costs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Selling,
general and administrative expense increased $18.0&nbsp;million, or 12%, to $167.0&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $149.0&nbsp;million
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. This included an increase of $11.4&nbsp;million of reorganization expenses that are primarily post-employment benefits related to executive
resignation agreements. It also included an increase of $5.6&nbsp;million in office-related expenses such as lease expense, maintenance, utilities and supplies primarily related to the expansion of
our document review centers' capacity, and an increase of $1.9&nbsp;million related to our strategic and financial review process. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation
and software and leasehold amortization increased $5.0&nbsp;million, or 16%, to $36.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $31.0&nbsp;million
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, as a result of increased depreciation on equipment and software related to capital expenditures. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Amortization
of identifiable intangible assets decreased $6.1&nbsp;million, or 33% to $12.7&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $18.8&nbsp;million during
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease was the result of applying an accelerated amortization method to certain of our intangible assets that are at later stages of their estimated
useful lives. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair
value adjustment to contingent consideration of $1.1&nbsp;million and $2.6&nbsp;million were recorded during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively,
related to our acquisition of De Novo Legal LLC in 2011. See Note&nbsp;9 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion of the contingent consideration. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Interest Expense  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense increased $4.6&nbsp;million, or 37%, to $16.7&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from
$12.1&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The increase reflects the higher principal amount of debt outstanding during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 as compared to
the prior year and the higher rate of interest for our term loan under the credit facility as compared to the interest rate under the former credit facility. Interest expense for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014 included $0.8&nbsp;million related to fees incurred and expensed in conjunction with the amendment to our credit facility. Interest expense for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2013 included $1.0&nbsp;million for the write-off of fees related to the early termination of the former credit facility. See Note&nbsp;5 to the Consolidated Financial
Statements for further discussion of the credit facility. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Income Taxes  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our effective tax rate for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 was 77.2% compared to 35.0% for the prior year end. Our 2014
effective tax rate was higher than the U.S. statutory rate primarily because of the relative mix of income earned in international jurisdictions compared to the pre-tax loss in the United States. In
2014, the tax rate used in computing the tax benefit on U.S. losses was significantly higher than the tax rate used in computing the tax expense on foreign income, which resulted in an overall
effective tax rate that was not customary. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Technology Segment  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating revenue increased $12.8&nbsp;million, or 4%, to $297.7&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from
$284.9&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The increase in revenue was primarily the result of growth in our Europe and Asia operations, which increased $11.0&nbsp;million
or 22% as compared to 2013, including an increase of $5.4&nbsp;million related to ESI. In addition, ESI revenue increased by $3.2&nbsp;million in our North America operations, offset by a decrease
in document review services of $1.4&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue
from reimbursable expenses was unchanged at $2.5&nbsp;million for both the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Direct
costs, selling, general and administrative expenses increased $19.8&nbsp;million, or 10%, to $218.3&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from
$198.5&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. This included an $11.2&nbsp;million increase in direct compensation expenses for employees, project-based attorneys and
contractor labor. This direct compensation increase was partially offset by a $6.7&nbsp;million decrease in general and administrative employee compensation. The change in Direct costs, selling,
general and administrative expenses also included a $7.9&nbsp;million increase in information technology-related costs, a $3.8&nbsp;million increase in other production related costs, and a
$3.3&nbsp;million increase in office-related expenses such as lease expense, maintenance, utilities and supplies primarily related to the expansion of our document review centers' capacity. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration Segment  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating revenue decreased $7.4&nbsp;million, or 5%, to $146.4&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from
$153.8&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease was primarily due to a $10.6&nbsp;million decrease in settlement administration revenues driven by a large private
anti-trust engagement in the prior year which was completed in 2013 that increased legal notification and advertising services for that period. Settlement administration continues to be dependent on
the timing and size of contracts awarded. This decrease was offset by a $3.2&nbsp;million increase in bankruptcy related revenues in 2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue
from reimbursable expenses decreased $13.1&nbsp;million, or 32%, to $27.8&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $40.9&nbsp;million during the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, primarily due to a decrease in reimbursable postage costs. Our direct costs associated with reimbursable expenses are included in Direct costs, selling, general
and administrative expenses in the table above. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Direct
costs, selling, general and administrative expenses decreased $24.5&nbsp;million, or 17%, to $121.1&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from
$145.6&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease was primarily the result of a $20.7&nbsp;million decrease in direct cost of services which was related to the large
private anti-trust engagement which was active during 2013. In addition, there was a $3.1&nbsp;million decrease in general and administrative employee compensation costs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Liquidity and Capital Resources  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Overview  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We had $27.6&nbsp;million in cash and cash equivalents as of December&nbsp;31, 2015, of which $10.0&nbsp;million was held by our
foreign subsidiaries at financial institutions outside of the United States. We consider the earnings of our foreign subsidiaries to be indefinitely invested outside the United States on the basis of
estimates that future domestic cash generation will be sufficient to meet future domestic cash needs. As of December&nbsp;31, 2015, our earnings in accordance with U.S.&nbsp;GAAP in excess of the
tax basis of our investments in foreign subsidiaries were $35.3&nbsp;million. In the event that we decide to repatriate foreign earnings, we would have to adjust the income tax provision in the
period when we determine that the earnings will no longer be indefinitely invested outside the United States. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>36</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>

<A NAME="page_do12601_1_37"> </A>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A HREF="#bg12601a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
have historically funded our operations primarily through cash flows from operations and borrowings under our credit facility. Furthermore, we have historically used cash to develop
and enhance our proprietary software products, fund our capital expenditures, repurchase shares of our common stock, pay dividends and acquire businesses. We have also used cash to pay interest and
principal amounts outstanding under various debt agreements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
believe that existing cash balances and other current assets, together with cash provided by operating activities and, as necessary, borrowing capacity under our credit facility, will
be sufficient to meet our expected operating and debt service requirements for at least the next 12&nbsp;months. As we expect to continue to generate positive free cash flow in 2016 and beyond, we
expect to continue to repay or be able to refinance the amounts outstanding under our credit facility as or before they become due and payable. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Operating Activities  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, our operating activities provided net cash of $81.3&nbsp;million. Included in net
cash provided by operating activities was a net loss of $11.9&nbsp;million, which included $98.9&nbsp;million of non-cash expenses for a total contribution to operating cash flows of
$87.0&nbsp;million related to net income adjusted to exclude non-cash expenses. Cash provided by operating activities also included a $5.7&nbsp;million net use of cash resulting from changes in
operating
assets and liabilities, primarily from an $8.6&nbsp;million increase in trade accounts receivable and a $3.0&nbsp;million increase in other current assets offset by a $5.7&nbsp;million decrease
in accounts payable and other liabilities and a decrease of $0.2&nbsp;million in refundable income taxes. Trade accounts receivable fluctuate from period to period depending on the period to period
change in revenue and the timing of revenue and collections. Accounts payable fluctuate from period to period depending on the timing of purchases and payments. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, our operating activities provided net cash of $69.7&nbsp;million. Included in net cash provided by operating activities was a net loss
of $1.3&nbsp;million, which included $67.3&nbsp;million of non-cash expenses for a total contribution to operating cash flows of $66.0&nbsp;million related to net income adjusted to exclude
non-cash expenses. Cash provided by operating activities also included a $3.7&nbsp;million net increase in cash resulting from changes in operating assets and liabilities, primarily from a
$22.5&nbsp;million decrease in trade accounts receivable, offset by an increase in income taxes receivable of $11.7&nbsp;million and a decrease in accounts payable and other liabilities of
$3.9&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, our operating activities provided net cash of $32.6&nbsp;million. Included in net cash provided by operating activities was net income
of $11.1&nbsp;million and $58.1&nbsp;million of non-cash expenses, for a total of $69.2&nbsp;million. Cash provided by operating activities also included a $36.6&nbsp;million net use of cash
resulting from changes in operating assets and liabilities, primarily from a $43.4&nbsp;million increase in trade accounts receivable including a $32.7&nbsp;million increase in fourth quarter
total revenue as compared to the same period in the prior year. Cash provided by operating activities also included the use of cash for client deposits primarily related to the fourth quarter 2012
receipt of a $14.3&nbsp;million client deposit for a large settlement administration engagement and other expenditures for that matter. These uses of cash were partially offset by a
$16.1&nbsp;million increase in accounts payable and other liabilities and a $5.9&nbsp;million increase in income tax liabilities. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Investing Activities  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 and 2014, we used $124.6&nbsp;million to fund the acquisition of Iris and
$0.3&nbsp;million to fund the acquisition of Minus 10, respectively. We used $19.9&nbsp;million, $28.9&nbsp;million and $34.6&nbsp;million during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014
and 2013, respectively, to fund purchases of property and equipment, primarily computer hardware for our </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>37</FONT></P>

Financing Activities  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, we borrowed $98.0&nbsp;million under our credit facility to fund a portion of the
purchase consideration related to the Iris acquisition. We also paid $37.1&nbsp;million of principal amounts related to our debt, including $27.0&nbsp;million related to our credit facility,
$4.6&nbsp;million related to a note payable and $5.4&nbsp;million related to capital lease obligations. We paid $1.7&nbsp;million of debt issuance cost in conjunction with the second and third
amendments to our Credit Agreement. We paid $13.2&nbsp;million in dividends and used $4.2&nbsp;million to repurchase shares of common stock to satisfy employee tax withholding obligations upon the
vesting of restricted stock awards and certain stock option exercises. Cash proceeds from the exercise of stock options were $3.9&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, we paid $10.8&nbsp;million of principal amounts related to our debt, including $3.0&nbsp;million related to our credit facility,
$4.1&nbsp;million related to notes payable and $3.7&nbsp;million related to capital lease obligations. We also paid $5.0&nbsp;million of contingent purchase consideration related to the
December&nbsp;28, 2011 acquisition of De Novo Legal LLC based upon achievement of 2013 revenue-based performance measures, $12.8&nbsp;million in dividends and we used $4.0&nbsp;million to
repurchase shares of common stock to satisfy employee tax withholding obligations upon the vesting of restricted stock awards and certain stock option exercises. Additionally, we used
$0.8&nbsp;million related to debt issuance costs. Cash proceeds from the exercise of stock options were $12.5&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we borrowed $88.0&nbsp;million and repaid $287.0&nbsp;million under our former credit facility, inclusive of the payment of the
outstanding revolving loan balance on August&nbsp;27, 2013, the proceeds of which were used primarily to fund working capital requirements associated with sequential revenue growth and capital
expenditures including the Kansas City corporate headquarters expansion and the data center consolidation project. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we paid $3.1&nbsp;million of
contingent purchase consideration related to the December&nbsp;28, 2011 acquisition of De Novo Legal LLC, $7.9&nbsp;million of principal payments related to other debt, and $12.9&nbsp;million of
dividends. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we used $29.4&nbsp;million to repurchase shares under the 2012 Program (as defined below) and to satisfy employee tax withholding
obligations upon the vesting of restricted stock awards and certain stock option exercises. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Credit Agreement  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In August 2013, we entered into a $400&nbsp;million senior secured credit facility, which originally consisted of a
$100&nbsp;million senior revolving loan commitment, maturing in August 2018, and a $300&nbsp;million senior secured term loan, maturing in August 2020 (the "Credit Agreement"). The credit facility
is secured by liens on our real property and a significant portion of our personal property. Our Credit Agreement also provides a $200&nbsp;million uncommitted Accordion for access to incremental
capital. The Accordion provides for increasing the senior secured term loan from the original $300&nbsp;million up to $500&nbsp;million and/or increasing the total capacity under the senior
revolving loan commitment from its original $100&nbsp;million up to a maximum of $200&nbsp;million with the aggregate total increase in the term loan and revolving loans not to exceed
$200&nbsp;million. In April 2015, we utilized a portion of the borrowing capacity under the Accordion, and as a result, increased the borrowings outstanding under the senior secured term loan by
$75&nbsp;million, with the net proceeds used to fund a portion of the purchase consideration for Iris. As of December&nbsp;31, 2015, we have $125&nbsp;million of </FONT></P>

<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


<U>Credit Agreement Amendments</U> </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> First Amendment:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March&nbsp;26, 2014, we entered into the First Amendment to the Credit Agreement ("First
Amendment"), which reduced the interest rate options for our senior secured term loan and reduced the LIBOR floor for an aggregate reduction of 50 basis points. Effective with the date of the First
Amendment, the senior secured term loan bore interest as follows: (1)&nbsp;2.50% plus prime rate subject to a 1.75% floor; or (2)&nbsp;3.50% plus one, two, three or six month LIBOR subject to a
0.75% LIBOR floor, for an aggregate floating rate floor of 4.25%. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Second Amendment:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On January&nbsp;26, 2015, we entered into the Second Amendment to the Credit Agreement (the "Second
Amendment"), which increased the senior secured term loan interest rate options by 25 basis points to the following: (1)&nbsp;2.75% plus prime rate subject to a 1.75% floor; or (2)&nbsp;3.75% plus
one, two, three or six month LIBOR subject to a 0.75% LIBOR floor, for an aggregate floating rate floor of 4.50%. The Second Amendment also amended the definition of "Applicable Margin" increasing the
margin determined by reference to our consolidated net leverage ratio (as defined in the Credit Agreement) for purposes of calculating the interest rate for base rate loans, Eurodollar loans and the
fee applicable to letters of credit as specified therein. In addition, the Second Amendment amended the definitions of "Consolidated EBITDA", "Consolidated Net Income" and "Excess Cash Flow" to permit
us to add back the additional following charges: (1)&nbsp;severance and reorganization costs and expenses incurred during any trailing twelve month period that includes a fiscal quarter ending on or
after January&nbsp;1, 2014 and on or prior to December&nbsp;31, 2014; and (2)&nbsp;certain fees, costs and expenses incurred by us in connection with our previously announced review of certain
strategic and financial alternatives, including potential proxy contests. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Third Amendment:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On April&nbsp;30, 2015, we entered into the Third Amendment to the Credit Agreement (the "Third
Amendment") to exercise our right under the $200&nbsp;million Accordion increasing the borrowings outstanding under the senior secured term loan by an aggregate principal amount of
$75&nbsp;million. As a result of the Third Amendment, we have the right, subject to compliance with the covenants specified in the Credit Agreement, to increase the borrowing capacity under the
revolving credit facility by $125&nbsp;million. The Third Amendment also provides for repayment of borrowings outstanding under the senior secured term loan in 21 quarterly payments of principal of
$0.9&nbsp;million, commencing on June&nbsp;30, 2015, with the remaining principal balance of the term loan due upon the maturity date in August 2020. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
addition, the Credit Agreement contains certain annual mandatory prepayment terms based on a percentage of excess cash flow. Excess cash flow, as defined in the Credit Agreement,
consists of Consolidated EBITDA (as defined in the Credit Agreement) adjusted for capital expenditures, changes in working capital, interest paid, income taxes paid, principal payments, dividends and
certain acquisition-related obligations. Such annual mandatory prepayments are required when the applicable year end net leverage ratio exceeds 2.75 to 1.00 and any payments reduce proportionately the
remaining quarterly principal payments. During the first quarter of 2015, we made a $0.6&nbsp;million excess cash flow payment relating to the period ending December&nbsp;31, 2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Credit Agreement contains a financial covenant related to a net leverage ratio (as defined in the Credit Agreement) which is not permitted to exceed 4.50 to 1.00 as well as other
customary covenants related to limitations on (i)&nbsp;creating liens, debt, guarantees or other contingent obligations, (ii)&nbsp;engaging in mergers, acquisitions and consolidations,
(iii)&nbsp;prepaying, redeeming or repurchasing subordinated or junior debt, and (iv)&nbsp;engaging in certain transactions with affiliates, in each case, subject to customary exceptions. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Under
our Credit Agreement, our ability to declare and pay dividends and repurchase securities from equity holders is limited by a requirement that such payments are not to exceed, in
the aggregate, 50% of net income, as adjusted, on a cumulative basis for all quarterly periods from the closing date of the credit facility and ending prior to the date of payment or repurchase.
Adjustments to Consolidated Net Income (as defined in the Credit Agreement) include among other items, the exclusion of extraordinary items, specified severance costs, cumulative effect of a change in
accounting principle, intangible asset amortization and impairment charges, non-cash compensation expense, cumulative effect of foreign currency translations, and gains or losses from discontinued
operations. Further, we are not allowed to declare and pay dividends and repurchase securities from equity holders if our net leverage ratio on a pro forma basis would exceed 4.25 to 1.0 or if our pro
forma unused capacity on the senior revolving loan would be less than $25&nbsp;million. The amounts outstanding under the credit facility may be accelerated upon the occurrence of an event of
default under the Credit Agreement. </FONT></P>

credit outstanding that reduce the borrowing capacity under the senior revolving loan. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>

Business Acquisitions  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On April&nbsp;30, 2015, Epiq completed the acquisition of all of the capital stock of Iris pursuant to a Stock Purchase Agreement
dated April&nbsp;7, 2015 (the "Purchase Agreement"). </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Under
the terms of the Purchase Agreement, the aggregate purchase consideration was $133.8&nbsp;million (the "Purchase Consideration"), consisting of $124.7&nbsp;million in cash
consideration ("Cash Consideration") and $9.1&nbsp;million of assumed capital lease obligations of the seller. The Cash Consideration was funded with existing cash and borrowings under our Credit
Agreement. Of the Cash Consideration, $68.6&nbsp;million was paid to the seller at closing, and $55.2&nbsp;million was distributed by Iris to participants in the Amended and Restated Iris Data
Services, Inc. Participation Plan (the "Plan"), in accordance with the terms of the Plan and the Purchase Agreement. The remaining Cash Consideration of $0.9&nbsp;million was paid to the seller and
participants in the Plan during the three months ended September&nbsp;30, 2015. The distributions to the participants in the Plan resulted in post-closing tax benefits to Epiq of approximately
$23.0&nbsp;million. In addition, of the Cash Consideration, approximately $13.0&nbsp;million was placed in escrow for fifteen months after the closing as security for potential future
indemnification claims. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
April&nbsp;1, 2014, we completed the acquisition of Minus 10, a company that develops and maintains software products and provides related services to its clients with respect to
web-enabled bankruptcy preparation and case management and expanded our Chapter&nbsp;11 restructuring service offerings. The combined purchase consideration of $1.3&nbsp;million included
$0.3&nbsp;million in cash consideration, $0.1&nbsp;million of deferred purchase price and contingent consideration with an acquisition date fair value of $0.9&nbsp;million. During the second
quarter of 2015, we remeasured the fair value of the contingent consideration using actual operating results and our revised forecasted operating results for Minus 10 for the remainder of the
measurement period. As a result of this remeasurement, the fair </FONT></P>

Dividends  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our Board declared quarterly cash dividends of $0.09 per common share in each of the four quarters of 2015, 2014 and 2013, and
representing $13.5&nbsp;million, $13.0&nbsp;million and $12.8&nbsp;million, respectively, in total dividends. Total dividends paid during 2015, 2014, and 2013 were $13.2&nbsp;million,
$12.8&nbsp;million and $12.9&nbsp;million, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
November&nbsp;5, 2015, the Board declared a cash dividend of $0.09 per outstanding share of common stock to shareholders of record as of the close of business on January&nbsp;7,
2016. On February&nbsp;16, 2016, we paid $3.3&nbsp;million of dividends to holders of our common stock related to the November&nbsp;5, 2015 declaration date. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
February&nbsp;25, 2016, the Board declared a cash dividend of $0.09 per outstanding share of common stock payable on May&nbsp;2, 2016 to shareholders of record as of the close of
business on April&nbsp;4, 2016. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
do not have a formal dividend policy. We determine if we will pay cash dividends on a quarterly basis and dividends may be declared at the discretion of our Board. There is no
assurance that we will continue to pay cash dividends on our common stock in the future, or that any such dividends will be comparable to those previously declared. Any future declarations of
dividends and the establishment of future record and payment dates are subject to the final determination of our Board. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Share Repurchase Program  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On November&nbsp;6, 2013, our Board approved and authorized the 2014 Share Repurchase Program, which allowed us to repurchase, on or
prior to December&nbsp;31, 2015, outstanding
shares of our common stock up to an aggregate of $35.0&nbsp;million. The 2014 Share Repurchase Program became effective on January&nbsp;1, 2014 and expired on December&nbsp;31, 2015. There were
no repurchases of shares of common stock made under the 2014 Share Repurchase Program. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
June&nbsp;1, 2012, our Board authorized the repurchase, through December&nbsp;31, 2013, of up to an aggregate of $35.0&nbsp;million of our outstanding shares of common stock
(the "2012 Program"). During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we purchased 1,768,296&nbsp;shares of common stock under the 2012 Program for $22.9&nbsp;million, at an average cost of $12.94
per share. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>



<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Capital Expenditures  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal years 2015, 2014 and 2013 our capital expenditures, inclusive of assets funded by capital leases and notes payable, were
$35.6&nbsp;million, $40.9&nbsp;million and $48.6&nbsp;million, respectively. We have made significant investments to expand our global data centers and upgrade our network infrastructure in the
United States and our international locations in order to support our global growth in client data volumes and to enhance client data security. We expect to continue to make capital expenditure
investments in our operations including in our acquired businesses. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>



<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Off-balance Sheet Arrangements  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not utilize off-balance sheet arrangements in our operations; however, we enter into operating leases in the ordinary course of
business. Our operating lease obligations are disclosed below under "Contractual Obligations" and also in Note&nbsp;6 to the Consolidated Financial Statements. </FONT></P>

Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our Consolidated Financial Statements are prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States,
which require management to make estimates, judgments and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in our Consolidated Financial Statements and accompanying notes. We believe our most critical
accounting policies and estimates relate to the following:</FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Revenue recognition </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Recoverability of goodwill </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Recoverability of long-lived assets </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Income taxes </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>
<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>42</FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Management
has discussed the development, selection and disclosure of critical accounting policies and estimates with the Audit Committee of the Board. While our estimates and
assumptions are based on our knowledge of current events and actions we may undertake in the future, actual results may ultimately differ from these estimates and assumptions. For a discussion of our
significant accounting policies, refer to Note&nbsp;1 to the Consolidated Financial Statements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>



<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Revenue Recognition  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have arrangements with clients pursuant to which we provide multiple elements of services that are billed based on unit prices and
volumes for which we have identified each deliverable service element. Based on our evaluation of each element, we have determined that each element delivered has stand-alone value to our clients
because we or other vendors sell such services separately from any other services and deliverables. However, we don't sell these services on a stand-alone basis in sufficient volumes to establish
evidence of fair value. Therefore, we obtain objective and reliable evidence of the fair value of each element based on third-party evidence of similar services or, for elements where third-party
evidence cannot be established, the best estimate of sales price has been used. Our arrangements do not include general rights of return. Accordingly, each of the service elements in our multiple
element case and document management arrangements qualifies as a separate unit of accounting. We allocate revenue to the various units of accounting in our arrangements based on the fair value or best
estimated selling price of each unit of accounting, which is generally consistent with the stated prices in our arrangements. In instances when revenue recognition is deferred, we utilize the relative
selling price method to calculate the revenue recognized for each period. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
recognize revenue for each service deliverable when the following criteria are satisfied: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> we have evidence of an arrangement, </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> the services are rendered, </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> our fee becomes fixed and determinable, and </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> collectability is reasonably assured. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Payments
received in advance of satisfaction of the related revenue recognition criteria are recognized as a client deposit until all revenue recognition criteria have been satisfied. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Recoverability of Goodwill  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Goodwill consists of the excess of cost of acquired enterprises over the sum of the amounts assigned to identifiable assets acquired
less liabilities assumed. We assess goodwill for impairment on at least an annual basis, as of July&nbsp;31, at a reporting unit level and have identified our operating segments (Technology and
Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration) as our reporting units for purposes of testing for goodwill impairment. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our
goodwill impairment test consists of a two-step process. The first step is to compare the fair value of a reporting unit to its carrying value, including goodwill. We considered both
a market approach and an income approach in order to develop an estimate of the fair value of each reporting unit for purposes of our annual impairment test. When available, and as appropriate, we use
market multiples derived from a set of competitors or companies with comparable market characteristics to establish fair values for a particular reporting unit (market approach). We also estimate fair
value using discounted projected cash flow analysis (income approach). Potential impairment is indicated when the carrying value of a reporting unit, including goodwill, exceeds its estimated fair
value. This analysis requires significant judgments, including estimation of future cash flows, which is dependent on internal forecasts, estimation of the long-term rate of growth for our business,
estimation of the useful life over which cash flows will occur, and determination of our weighted average cost of capital. Changes in </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>43</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>
<!-- ZEQ.=8,SEQ=46,EFW="2227381",CP="EPIQ SYSTEMS,INC.",DN="1",CHK=70260,FOLIO='43',FILE='DISK134:[15ZCW1.15ZCW12601]DO12601A.;12',USER='ABEAULI',CD='26-FEB-2016;15:12' -->
<A NAME="page_do12601_1_44"> </A>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A HREF="#bg12601a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>these
estimates and assumptions could materially affect the determination of fair value and goodwill impairment for each reporting unit. In addition, financial and credit market volatility directly
impacts our fair value measurement through our weighted average cost of capital, used to determine our discount rate, and through our stock price, used to determine our market capitalization. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
second step compares the implied fair value of the reporting unit's goodwill with the carrying amount of that goodwill. If the carrying amount of the reporting unit's goodwill
exceeds its implied fair value, an impairment charge is recognized in an amount equal to that excess. The loss recognized cannot exceed the carrying amount of goodwill. As of July&nbsp;31, 2015,
which is the date of our most recent impairment test, the fair value of each of our reporting units was in excess of the carrying value of the reporting unit. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
following table illustrates the percentages by which each reporting unit's fair value and our aggregate fair value exceeded its carrying value as of July&nbsp;31, 2015. In
addition, the table includes a sensitivity analysis related to changes in certain key assumptions as noted below for each reporting unit. The impact of each assumption change within the sensitivity
analysis was calculated independently and excludes the impact of the other assumed changes. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As
of December&nbsp;31, 2015, there have been no events since our last annual test to indicate that it is more likely than not that the recorded goodwill balance had become impaired.
As of December&nbsp;31, 2015, goodwill for the Technology and Bankruptcy and Settlement Administration reporting units was $262.5&nbsp;million and $215.0&nbsp;million, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Recoverability of Long-lived Assets  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We amortize long-lived assets over their estimated useful lives. Identifiable long-lived assets are reviewed for impairment whenever
events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying value may not be recoverable. Determination of recoverability is based on the lowest level of identifiable estimated undiscounted future
cash flows resulting from use of the asset and its eventual disposition. Measurement of any impairment loss is based on the excess of the carrying value of the asset over its fair value. Fair value is
determined based on the lowest level of identifiable estimated future cash flows using discount rates determined by our management to be commensurate with the risk inherent in our business model. Our
estimates of future cash flows attributable to our long-lived assets require significant judgment based on our historical and anticipated results and are subject to many factors. Different assumptions
and judgments could materially affect estimated future cash flows relating to our long-lived assets which could trigger impairment. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Income Taxes  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our annual income tax expense or benefit is impacted by our income and the statutory tax rates and tax planning opportunities available
to us in the various jurisdictions in which we operate. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>44</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>
<!-- ZEQ.=9,SEQ=47,EFW="2227381",CP="EPIQ SYSTEMS,INC.",DN="1",CHK=1025013,FOLIO='44',FILE='DISK134:[15ZCW1.15ZCW12601]DO12601A.;12',USER='ABEAULI',CD='26-FEB-2016;15:12' -->
<A NAME="page_do12601_1_45"> </A>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A HREF="#bg12601a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Significant
judgment is required in determining our annual tax expense and in evaluating our tax positions. We establish reserves to remove some or all of the tax benefit of any of our tax positions
at the time we determine that the positions become uncertain based upon one of the following: (1)&nbsp;the tax position is not "more likely than not" to be sustained, (2)&nbsp;the tax position is
"more likely than not" to be sustained, but for a lesser amount, or (3)&nbsp;the tax position is "more likely than not" to be sustained, but not in the financial period in which the tax position was
originally taken. For purposes of evaluating whether or not a tax position is uncertain, (1)&nbsp;we presume the tax position will be examined by the
relevant taxing authority that has full knowledge of all relevant information, (2)&nbsp;the technical merits of a tax position are derived from authorities such as legislation and statutes,
legislative intent, regulations, rulings and case law and their applicability to the facts and circumstances of the tax position, and (3)&nbsp;each tax position is evaluated without considerations
of the possibility of offset or aggregation with other tax positions taken. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Tax
law requires items to be recognized in our tax returns differently than how these items are reflected in the Consolidated Financial Statements. As a result, the annual tax rate
reflected in our Consolidated Financial Statements is different from that reported in our tax returns (our cash tax rate). Some of these differences are permanent, such as expenses that are not
deductible in our tax returns, and some differences reverse over time, such as depreciation expense. These timing differences create deferred tax assets and liabilities. Deferred tax assets and
liabilities are determined based on temporary differences between the financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities. The tax rates used to measure deferred tax assets or liabilities are
the enacted tax rates in effect for the current year and take into account the manner and timing in which the differences are expected to reverse in the future. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Valuation
allowances are recorded against our deferred tax assets when it is more likely than not (greater than 50%) that a tax benefit will not be realized. In evaluating our ability to
recover our deferred tax assets in the jurisdiction from which they arise, we consider all available positive and negative evidence. Positive evidence includes factors such as a history of profitable
operations and projections of future profitability within the carryforward period, including taxable income from tax planning strategies. Negative evidence includes items such as historical cumulative
losses, projections of future losses, or carryforward periods that are not long enough to allow for the utilization of a deferred tax asset based on our projections of future taxable income.
Historical operating income or loss provide objective evidence, and we consider three years of historical cumulative pretax losses to be a compelling factor in recording a valuation allowance. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred
tax assets, for which no valuation allowance is recorded, may not be realized upon changes in facts and circumstances, resulting in a future charge to establish a valuation
allowance. Existing valuation allowances are re-examined under the same standards of positive and negative evidence at each period end. If it is determined that it is more likely than not that a
deferred tax asset will be realized, the appropriate amount of the valuation allowance, if any, is released. </FONT></P>
